clue.text: Arrive holding note for Lefty

indicators.note: the verb for arriving keeps the musical note held within its letters

parts.note: to arrive is to come
MI is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone turns up bringing a written message for a left-handed friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lefty' looks like a nickname, but it is the definition: an informal word for a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A lefty is slang for a left-wing radical, and a commie is slang for a communist, the same political type.

clue.text: Ring to authorise identification

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
to authorise a document is to sign it

explanation.surface: A phone call made to approve an identity check.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio station's call sign is the code that identifies it on air.

clue.text: Musician with 1200 pictures to marshal?

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is a thousand and CC two hundred
pictures as a body of work are art
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A musician with a huge stock of pictures to put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshal' looks like a verb meaning arrange; it is the noun, naming Napoleon's Marshal Ney.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney, songwriter of the Beatles, is a famous musician.

clue.text: One leader of Muslims? You can say that again

definitions.text: One leader of Muslims? You can say that again

parts.words: One leader of Muslims? You can say that again
parts.note: a prayer leader, whose title sounds like a contraction of 'I am' followed by 'am' a second time

explanation.surface: An exclamation of agreement after a question about a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M + AM, the title is 'I am' said twice over, which is what the stock phrase invites.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, a leader among Muslims.

clue.text: Woman's part, perhaps, one leading to contact with spies

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word part is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A role, maybe, that leads an actor into dealings with espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PART into PATR.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricia is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Very good character of chemical

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
the tone of something is its character or quality

explanation.surface: A chemical praised as having an excellent nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a colourless solvent, a chemical used in nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Try again to chant when practising play

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Actors repeat their chanting while practising a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is a legal trial, not an attempt: a court rehears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsing is going through a play in practice before performance.

clue.text: Volume published has great influence

parts.note: cl, a centilitre, is a measure of volume
a book that is published is out

explanation.surface: A newly issued book carries a lot of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is power or sway, especially political influence.

clue.text: Sailor and Turkish governors found religious houses

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A seaman and some Ottoman officials set up monasteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' means establish in the surface but is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbeys are monasteries or convents, homes of religious communities.

clue.text: A tongue somewhat colloquial in Guatemala

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A language spoken rather informally in a Central American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingua is Latin for language, as in lingua franca, a common tongue.

clue.text: Revictual sumptuously it's very profitable

indicators.note: restocking lavishly suggests the word's letters are piled up anew

explanation.surface: Restocking with food on a lavish scale pays very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sumptuously' rearranges REVICTUAL; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative business makes a lot of money.

clue.text: Henry's getting a lot of money for something very offensive

parts.note: the henry, symbol H, is the unit of inductance
a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in cost a bomb

explanation.surface: Henry is earning a fortune for something deeply rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' suggests rudeness but means an attack weapon. A 'bomb' is British slang for a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrogen bomb is a weapon of devastating attack, offensive in the military sense.

clue.text: Artist follows South American woman

indicators.note: follows puts the painter's letters after the continental abbreviation

parts.note: S and A abbreviate South and American
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter trails a woman from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Sara is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Buried in Arlington unknown — like this?

indicators.note: being buried in the cemetery jumbles the letters of its name

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unidentified soldier interred in the national cemetery, dying unaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buried in' rearranges ARLINGTON, and Y, an unknown, follows. The Unknown Soldier lies there, buried without anyone knowing who he was.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorantly means without knowledge, as the unknown dead lie unnamed.

clue.text: Be smoother when so?

indicators.note: the question hints that these letters need sorting out in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to calm down when you are being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BE SMOOTHER is what someone tiresome is told to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothersome means annoying, the sort of person told to calm down.

clue.text: Craft in lagoon, possibly carrying Doge originally

indicators.note: carrying puts the Doge's initial inside the rearranged letters
possibly signals that the word lagoon may be rearranged
originally picks the first letter of Doge

explanation.surface: A boat on the Venetian lagoon, perhaps with the Doge aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns LAGOON into GONOLA; 'carrying' puts D, from 'Doge originally', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian boat, a small craft.

clue.text: Flag makes some never-to be-forgotten signals

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A banner sends unforgettable messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points into 'forgotten signals', where the letters run across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag flown by a ship to show nationality.

clue.text: Good count upset by weight of explosive

indicators.note: upset tips the word count over into a new order

parts.note: a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: A nobleman, overturned, is crushed by a heavy load of explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns COUNT into UNCOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Guncotton is nitrocellulose, a high explosive.

clue.text: Rent up message about hard, long programme

indicators.note: about puts the letter for hard inside the turned-up message
in a down clue up turns each of the two words so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rent out is to let
a note is a short message
H is short for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A message about difficulty sent along by a long broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Sent', a misread of 'Rent' (LET). 'up' turns LET and NOTE in place to TEL and ETON; 'about' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity.

clue.text: Complaint-therefore holds back in extremes of perplexity

indicators.note: holds puts the turned-round pair inside the word for therefore

parts.note: thus means therefore

indicators.note: back reads the two outer letters from right to left
extremes of picks the first and last letters of perplexity

explanation.surface: A grumble: in consequence, someone hangs back, utterly perplexed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of perplexity' gives PY; 'back' makes it YP, held in THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhus is an infectious disease, and a complaint is an illness.

clue.text: Earnest sermon on debts

parts.note: ser is an abbreviation of sermon
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: A grave preacher speaks about money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious and earnest both mean sincere and solemn.

clue.text: Writer applied cane as a punishment

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: applied as in put to work in a new way, so the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author was beaten with a stick as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' rearranges CANE into ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering for wrongdoing, a form of punishment.

clue.text: Becoming fed up about fellow having had a cig

indicators.note: about turns the little word round

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man grows weary after his cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns UP to PU; 'Becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have puffed is to have drawn on a cigarette.

clue.text: House in Switzerland linked with weird tale

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: weird signals the letters of tale come out strangely ordered

explanation.surface: A Swiss house connected with a strange story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges TALE into ALET.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house of the Alpine kind.

clue.text: Modes of transport with special cushions for the bottom

definitions.text: Modes of transport with special cushions for the bottom

parts.words: Modes of transport with special cushions for the bottom
parts.note: the cushions sound like comfortable seat pads, but are the air on which these vehicles ride

explanation.surface: Vehicles fitted with comfy seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovercraft rides on a cushion of air trapped beneath its hull.

clue.text: Save a bit of petrol, perhaps, using this?

definitions.text: Save a bit of petrol, perhaps, using this?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters gathered here could be arranged otherwise
a bit of picks just the first letter of petrol

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a small scooter is economical on fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SAVE plus P, from 'a bit of petrol'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vespa is an Italian motor scooter, frugal with fuel.

clue.text: Archbishop returning in ceremonial garb

indicators.note: returning reads the signature from the end back to the start

parts.note: Ebor is the signature of the Archbishop of York

explanation.surface: A senior cleric comes back in his formal vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop of York signs as Ebor, from the Latin for York.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long formal gown worn at ceremonies.

clue.text: Colleague at work, and the reverse

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: the reverse means the same abbreviation again, turned round

parts.note: op, short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A workmate, and it works both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: OP, then OP backwards; 'oppo' is British slang for a mate or counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a close associate or opposite number at work.

clue.text: Girl has nothing with which to catch cattle

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A young woman with no possessions herds livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope thrown by cowboys to rope steers.

clue.text: Project too far above tar?

parts.note: over means above
pitch is a black tar

explanation.surface: Throwing something beyond its mark, on top of the tar.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to overpitch is to bowl the ball too far up the pitch, too near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpitch is to throw or bowl a ball beyond the ideal length.

clue.text: Rejected paintings and poetry, being cross

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: paintings are art
poetry is verse

explanation.surface: Angry that pictures and poems were turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but is the verb meaning to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across a place.

clue.text: How you might see rhino act at first, naturally?

definitions.text: How you might see rhino act at first, naturally?

indicators.note: act suggests the animal's name performs a rearrangement
at first takes only the opening letter of naturally

explanation.surface: Observing a rhinoceros behaving in its usual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' rearranges RHINO into HORNI; N is the first letter of 'naturally'. A rhino charges horn first, so it naturally intrudes.
explanation.definitionFit: To horn in is to intrude uninvited, as a charging horned beast would.
